title: Single backend runtime bootstrap contract
intent: Define the canonical apps/server NestJS bootstrap, global pipes, Swagger, tRPC middleware, shutdown, and local-first database startup behavior as a product requirement.
acceptance: AppModule composes every bounded service HTTP module through NestJS imports
bootstrap always installs global validation and Swagger/OpenAPI
tRPC Express middleware is mounted from NestJS bootstrap rather than a parallel server
shutdown closes TypeORM DataSource and server resources
manual_simulation: Start server with no DATABASE_URL, inspect OpenAPI and tRPC mounts, then repeat with DATABASE_URL and compare route availability.
incentive: Prevents backend split-brain and makes local-first startup testable.

title: HTTP and tRPC parity matrix for every API surface
intent: Require every public HTTP controller capability to have an equivalent tRPC/local-caller surface with shared service behavior and validation semantics.
acceptance: Every services/*/src/interface/http controller method is mapped to a tRPC procedure or explicitly documented as HTTP-only integration
CLI/TUI local callers can exercise workflow-critical APIs without HTTP
parity tests compare core response fields and errors
traceId propagation matches between HTTP and tRPC
anti_patterns: tRPC procedure directly querying TypeORM when HTTP delegates to service
missing local caller for workflow path
manual_simulation: For one workflow journey, call HTTP, tRPC, CLI caller, and TUI caller with same payload and compare trace/result/error shape.
incentive: Keeps web/CLI/TUI as invocation and visualization layers only.

title: Local-first PGlite to PostgreSQL switching PRD
intent: Specify database URL resolution, PGlite default storage, PostgreSQL override, PGlite socket mode, and migration behavior across all server and local callers.
acceptance: No DATABASE_URL creates managed local PGlite under FULCRUM_HOME
DATABASE_URL switches same TypeORM entities and migrations to PostgreSQL
PGlite socket explicit mode is covered by tests
database status is visible through doctor/API
anti_patterns: implicit in-memory database in product path
raw SQL migrations outside TypeORM classes
manual_simulation: Run migration/status checks under FULCRUM_HOME-only and DATABASE_URL modes, then compare entity counts and workflow route behavior.
incentive: Makes the local-first promise concrete without sacrificing production PostgreSQL.

title: TypeORM migration completeness and ordering PRD
intent: Define migration ownership, ordering, rollback expectations, and PGlite/PostgreSQL parity for all bounded service schemas.
acceptance: Every persisted entity is created by a TypeScript TypeORM migration
migration tests run on PGlite and PostgreSQL for critical schemas
no tracked .sql files exist
schema migration ledger records applied migrations and errors
anti_patterns: manual ALTER snippets in tests as product proof
manual_simulation: Apply fresh migrations on empty PGlite and PostgreSQL databases, then inspect ledger and run one CRUD path per service.
incentive: Prevents local-first database drift from blocking future service extraction.

title: Session and organization context API contract
intent: Specify how HTTP, tRPC, CLI, and TUI resolve user, org, session, and invitation context without duplicating auth logic.
acceptance: whoami returns stable user/org/session envelope
invitation accept/revoke paths enforce org scope
local session resolver uses same TypeORM data as HTTP auth
all service controllers accept org context consistently
anti_patterns: ad hoc orgId defaults in controllers
manual_simulation: Create org, invite user, accept invite, call whoami and org-scoped APIs from HTTP and local caller.
incentive: Tenant correctness is prerequisite for every local-first workflow.

title: Better Auth TypeORM adapter PRD
intent: Turn the Better Auth TypeORM adapter and passkey store into explicit product requirements covering PGlite limitations and PostgreSQL parity.
acceptance: adapter supports account/session/user verification CRUD through TypeORM
passkey registration and lookup work without direct database imports in app surfaces
PGlite transaction limitations are handled intentionally
PostgreSQL parity gate covers auth tables
anti_patterns: auth tests using production internals unnecessarily
manual_simulation: Register a passkey-backed user in PGlite, log in, reload session, then repeat against PostgreSQL.
incentive: Auth must not be the exception to the single TypeORM architecture.

title: Project public API full lifecycle PRD
intent: Define project list/create/load/update/delete/stats behavior, validation, tenant scope, and trace propagation through NestJS and tRPC.
acceptance: project CRUD preserves description, status, org, owner, and trace fields
stats endpoint aggregates real tasks and artifacts
HTTP and tRPC expose same project contract
PGlite and PostgreSQL persistence tests cover lifecycle
anti_patterns: web route direct work-management application imports
project list losing fields available in store
manual_simulation: Create project, add tasks, update metadata, load stats from HTTP/tRPC/CLI/TUI and verify same project state.
incentive: Project is the root of the workflow trace spine.

title: Task and work item command/query PRD
intent: Specify task CRUD, hierarchy, dependencies, manual workbench, CSV import/export, and trace behavior through the public API.
acceptance: tasks support create/list/load/update/delete with parent and dependency changes
manual workbench returns board/list/table-ready data without UI business logic
CSV import/export preserves fields and validation errors
traceId is accepted and returned for workflow entry points
manual_simulation: Import tasks, create dependency chain, update parent, open manual workbench, export CSV, then dispatch dependency run.
incentive: Tasks are the execution unit for human and agent workflows.

title: Task comment, watch, reaction, and notification PRD
intent: Define work item comment lifecycle, mention notification fanout, watcher behavior, and stream/update semantics.
acceptance: comments support create/list/update/resolve/delete with author scope
mentions create notification jobs
watch/reaction state is persisted through TypeORM
events are available to notification and subscription surfaces
anti_patterns: comment content parsed in UI only
manual_simulation: Comment with mention on a task, watch it, resolve thread, and verify notification and audit records.
incentive: Task collaboration must be real workflow state, not UI decoration.

title: Manual planning structure API PRD
intent: Capture sprint, cycle/module, saved view, intake, label, and PM structure endpoints needed for full manual PM parity.
acceptance: sprint CRUD supports task membership changes
cycle/module structure can be created, listed, and used in board filters
saved views persist filters, sort, and default status
manual PM surfaces can operate without AI
anti_patterns: board view hardcoded to tasks only
manual_simulation: Create sprint/module/view manually, assign tasks, switch board/list/table/calendar filters, and verify persisted state after reload.
incentive: Manual PM must stand alone before agent automation can be trusted.

title: Custom field and dependency validation PRD
intent: Specify public APIs for custom field definitions, field dependencies, bulk updates, and template interactions.
acceptance: field definitions preserve type, required, options, position, and config JSON
field dependency rules validate referenced fields and values
bulk task field changes return per-row success/failure
PGlite/PostgreSQL tests cover field schemas
anti_patterns: checkbox/boolean mapping drift between web and API
field IDs accepted across org boundary
manual_simulation: Create select field, add dependency, apply to tasks through API, and verify board/table rendering uses same values.
incentive: Custom fields unlock real PM workflows beyond fixed task columns.

title: Workflow automation and recurrence API PRD
intent: Define automation rules, recurrence schedules, template actions, validation, and execution event recording.
acceptance: automation templates and custom rules are discoverable
recurrence create/delete/list validates schedules and task scope
rule execution records audit and task mutations
automation works in PGlite and PostgreSQL
manual_simulation: Create recurring task rule, run scheduler tick, verify new task/audit/notification records and disable rule.
incentive: Recurring and automated work makes PM state durable without agent prompts.

title: Document public API workbench PRD
intent: Define document create/edit/detail/list/global-tree, templates, frontmatter, comments, backlinks, attachments, versions, and collaboration-state requirements.
acceptance: document CRUD preserves parent, project, type, body, editor JSON, frontmatter, and trace
template resolution is deterministic
comments/attachments/backlinks/versions are available via public API
global and project trees preserve sort and parent relationships
anti_patterns: attachments as metadata without storage policy
collaboration state not tied to document state
manual_simulation: Create nested docs, edit body/frontmatter, add comment/attachment/link, restore version, then start planning from doc.
incentive: Docs are first-class workflow context, not a side note store.

title: Real-time document collaboration API/runtime PRD
intent: Turn Yjs/Hocuspocus/Bun WebSocket collaboration scaffolding into explicit local-first requirements for docs editor convergence and persistence.
acceptance: two docs editor clients converge through Yjs under feature flag
provider dependencies are declared in package.json
Yjs snapshots persist to TypeORM and reload after restart
presence and cursor state are separate from saved document content
anti_patterns: mock provider counted as real collaboration proof
editor route showing presence without CRDT-bound content
task-only collaborative editor not wired to docs
manual_simulation: Open same doc in two clients, edit both offline/online, restart server, and verify converged saved content.
incentive: Closes a named W1 blocker with actual collaborative editing evidence.

title: Deterministic search and saved-search API PRD
intent: Specify document/memory/task search, suggestions, saved searches, snapshots, click feedback, PGlite fallback, and optional Meilisearch behavior.
acceptance: search, suggest, saved CRUD, click, and snapshot endpoints have DTO validation
PGlite full-text path is default and deterministic
optional backend dual-writes/fallbacks are feature flagged
saved search scope and ownership are enforced
anti_patterns: embeddings or semantic search introduced by default
manual_simulation: Index docs/tasks/memories, search and save query, break optional backend, and verify PGlite fallback stays correct.
incentive: Local-first search must work before optional intelligent retrieval.

title: Memory and context preview API PRD
intent: Define memory CRUD/search/digest and deterministic context preview requirements across docs, tasks, traces, and selected sources.
acceptance: memory CRUD enforces org and source refs
context preview is deterministic and cites included docs/tasks/memories
digest operation records inputs and outputs
CLI/TUI/web surfaces share response contract
anti_patterns: context preview reading raw app internals
manual_simulation: Create memories from docs and tasks, build context preview twice, and verify identical ordered source bundle.
incentive: Agent workflows need explainable context, not opaque retrieval.

title: Planning preview and materialization API PRD
intent: Define approved plan preview/materialize, freeform prompt/start, technical cycle generation, artifact execution, guided ACP start/action, and continuous update restart as one workflow API family.
acceptance: each planning endpoint accepts and returns traceId
materialize persists docs/tasks/dependencies/artifacts through TypeORM
artifact run uses service-owned sandbox runner
guided ACP action records traffic/session state
anti_patterns: planning route returns preview-only data for materialize
freeform docs not persisted before prompt
artifact execution shelling out from web route
ACP state stored only in UI
manual_simulation: Start from freeform doc, generate technical cycle, record artifact execution, materialize approved plan, then inspect docs/tasks/artifacts.
incentive: This is the start of the human and agent workflow journey.

title: End-to-end workflow acceptance cycle API PRD
intent: Specify the acceptance-cycle run endpoint as the trace-spine orchestrator from docs/context to plan, tasks, dependency execution, QA, review, UAT, and generated E2E.
acceptance: acceptance cycle consumes explicit project/docs/tasks inputs
every stage emits trace/audit events
partial failure returns recoverable state and next action
PGlite and PostgreSQL proofs cover persisted workflow state
anti_patterns: happy-path mock fixture as end-to-end proof
manual_simulation: Run acceptance cycle on a seeded project and follow resulting trace through planning, tasks, run events, QA, UAT, and E2E rows.
incentive: Turns Phase 9.6 into an auditable product workflow instead of disconnected endpoints.

title: Dependency run preview/dispatch/live feedback PRD
intent: Define dependency-aware execution endpoints, streaming feedback, lifecycle event recording, worker tick behavior, automated feedback loops, and QA review integration.
acceptance: preview returns ordered dependency tree and affected tasks
dispatch queues runs in dependency order with traceId
live-feedback stream and snapshot return compatible event shapes
worker tick records lifecycle output and retry/refusal state
anti_patterns: dispatch running tasks without previewable tree
SSE event shape differs from polling snapshot
worker tick mutates tasks without audit
manual_simulation: Create dependency chain, preview, dispatch, watch stream, run worker ticks, cancel/retry a run, and verify events.
incentive: Agent execution needs explainable ordering and live observability.

title: Review workbench and UAT API PRD
intent: Define review workbench preview/session save/load/annotate, final QA, feedback gate, UAT/code-review handoff/decision, and generated E2E run endpoints.
acceptance: review session persists diff tree, annotations, suggestions, and trace
final QA blocks handoff when open feedback remains
UAT decisions can be manual or configured auto-decision with audit
generated E2E run returns materialized test file metadata
anti_patterns: review annotations only in browser memory
final QA status not linked to trace
manual_simulation: Save review session, annotate diff, run final QA feedback gate, record UAT approval, generate E2E, and inspect artifacts.
incentive: Closes the human approval loop before agent handoff claims are made.

title: Audit query/export/retention API PRD
intent: Specify audit event query, export job/status, retention policy list/get/update, CSV/JSON formats, and local-first persistence.
acceptance: audit query filters by org, kind, subject, time, and trace
export returns CSV/JSON metadata and stable job status
retention policy update validates duration and scope
CLI/TUI can retrieve audit through configured API caller
anti_patterns: export building unbounded in memory without limits
manual_simulation: Generate task/run/review events, query by trace, export JSON and CSV, change retention, and verify old event handling.
incentive: Workflow supervision requires trustworthy audit trails.

title: Artifact lifecycle API PRD
intent: Define artifact upload/list/load/download/accept/reject/archive/unarchive/delete, retention, checksum, storage, and preview metadata requirements.
acceptance: artifact metadata includes project/task/run/body path/checksum/size/status
download endpoint never exposes unsafe paths
accept/reject/archive transitions emit audit events
PGlite and PostgreSQL tests cover metadata while filesystem storage remains local-first
anti_patterns: artifact body stored only in database blob without retention policy
manual_simulation: Upload artifact, preview/download, accept then archive/unarchive/delete, and verify audit plus filesystem effects.
incentive: Artifacts are the durable outputs of agent and human workflows.

title: Context trace persistence API PRD
intent: Define context-traces persist/load endpoints and trace summary behavior for linking docs, tasks, routes, runs, artifacts, memory, and audit events.
acceptance: context trace captures selected sources with stable source refs
load by traceId reconstructs source and output relationships
PGlite/PostgreSQL tests cover persistence and retrieval
workflow-cycle trace summary uses same storage
anti_patterns: trace summary recomputed only from current UI state
unstructured JSON without source type contracts
manual_simulation: Persist trace from docs/tasks/context, materialize workflow, load trace summary, and verify every source/output edge.
incentive: The trace spine is the core observability model for Phase 9.6.

title: Document workspace page-tree and operations preview PRD
intent: Specify page tree preview and page operations preview endpoints as service-owned equivalents to docs workbench behavior.
acceptance: page-tree preview preserves nesting, position, permissions, and breadcrumbs
page-operations preview covers rename/icon/delete/append/merge behavior
results match public document API tree semantics
drag-reorder acceptance references persisted move behavior
anti_patterns: preview using different tree sort than document API
manual_simulation: Build a nested page set, preview operations, perform equivalent API update, and compare rendered tree order.
incentive: Docs workbench needs tree operations that survive reloads and feed planning.

title: Agent run public API lifecycle PRD
intent: Define agent run list/load/dispatch/cancel/retry/status/candidate issue behavior with TypeORM persistence and workflow trace integration.
acceptance: dispatch creates run with project/task/trace/cwd/agent config metadata
cancel/retry transitions are idempotent and audited
candidate issues and state endpoints are filtered by org/project
PGlite and PostgreSQL persistence tests cover lifecycle
anti_patterns: run status inferred from transcript files only
cancel/retry mutating rows without lifecycle event
candidate issue query bypassing service boundary
manual_simulation: Dispatch run, load status, cancel, retry, attach lifecycle event, and verify trace/audit/artifacts.
incentive: Agent runs are first-class workflow entities, not background side effects.

title: Routing public API and rules engine PRD
intent: Specify routing draft, rule matching, auto-assign, fallback LLM, connector context, and public route behavior under Nest/service boundaries.
acceptance: routing API validates request context and returns explainable decision
rules engine hot reload has bounded failure behavior
LLM fallback is feature-flagged and never required for deterministic routing
routing events are emitted for audit/learning
anti_patterns: routing decision hidden in web route
rules loaded from multiple active sources
manual_simulation: Create rules, route a task/repo/context request, trigger no-match fallback, approve learned draft, and inspect event.
incentive: Routing governs which agent/tool acts, so decisions must be inspectable.

title: ACP session persistence and transport PRD
intent: Define ACP session store, traffic log, permission request/response, process/websocket transports, and guided planning session workbench requirements.
acceptance: sessions persist traceId, mode, model, cwd, permission mode, traffic, and status
permission prompts round-trip from live agent process to UI/API and back
transport abstraction covers stdio and websocket without changing session state
PGlite persistence proof covers session reload
anti_patterns: permission state only in browser memory
guided planning action not linked to ACP session
manual_simulation: Start guided ACP session, handle permission request, change mode/model, resume, cancel, and inspect persisted traffic.
incentive: ACP is the bridge between planning UI and real agents.

title: Notification public API and delivery runtime PRD
intent: Specify notification CRUD/read state/settings/rules/subscriptions plus webhook/SMTP/push/in-app delivery semantics.
acceptance: notifications list/read/mute/settings endpoints enforce org/user scope
delivery worker records attempts, retries, and terminal failures
webhook/SMTP/push handlers share delivery result contract
read state persists through PGlite and PostgreSQL
anti_patterns: rule channels stored in driver-specific format without tests
manual_simulation: Create notification rule, emit task mention event, run delivery worker, mark read, and inspect retries/failures.
incentive: Users need durable feedback from long-running workflows.

title: Subscription event stream PRD
intent: Define server-side subscription stream, EventBus, database notify bridge, polling fallback, CLI/TUI bridge, and browser SSE/WebSocket expectations.
acceptance: subscription API exposes topic-scoped stream with auth and backpressure policy
PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY bridge publishes same event shape as polling fallback
PGlite uses polling fallback within documented latency
CLI/TUI subscription bridge receives events within threshold
anti_patterns: SSE only for one route family
PGlite path silently disables live updates
manual_simulation: Subscribe to task/run/notification topics in PostgreSQL and PGlite modes, emit events, and verify same payloads arrive.
incentive: Live supervision needs one event model across local and production databases.

title: Settings, feature flags, experiments, and theme API PRD
intent: Define settings/feature flag/experiment/theme APIs, config parsing, per-org scope, and safe defaults for optional features.
acceptance: settings reads/writes are org-scoped and schema validated
feature flags expose default/off behavior and audit changes
experiments have enrollment and metrics contract
theme settings persist and load across surfaces
anti_patterns: environment flags overriding persisted org settings unexpectedly
feature-enabled code imported when flag off
theme settings stored in web local storage only
manual_simulation: Toggle a feature flag and theme, reload web/CLI/TUI status, and verify optional code paths stay off by default.
incentive: Optional capabilities need local-first controls without hidden behavior drift.

title: Doctor and readiness public API PRD
intent: Specify health/readiness checks for API, CLI, TUI, routing, inference, database, skills, hooks, and subscriptions.
acceptance: doctor endpoint returns structured status, severity, message, recovery
database and migration state are included
routing/inference/subscription checks have bounded timeouts
CLI/TUI doctor use same check definitions or API callers
anti_patterns: doctor output parsed from human text
manual_simulation: Break database URL, disable inference backend, add routing conflict, run doctor via API/CLI/TUI, and compare recoveries.
incentive: Users need precise local runtime diagnosis before workflows fail mid-run.

title: Credential and secrets API PRD
intent: Define credential storage, keyring/vault adapters, secret doctor checks, API redaction, and agent/runtime access policies.
acceptance: credential API never returns secret values after creation
local keyring/vault fallback behavior is documented and tested
credential use emits audit-safe references
secret doctor checks detect missing backend and recovery
anti_patterns: secrets in logs or audit payloads
raw credential entity returned by controller
one adapter silently replacing another without status
manual_simulation: Create credential, use it from connector/inference path, verify response redaction and doctor status, then delete/rotate.
incentive: Local-first integrations still need strict secret boundaries.

title: Inference public API and backend lifecycle PRD
intent: Define inference routing, provider credentials, model metadata, backend probes, streaming/pull progress, embedded/local backend behavior, and health checks.
acceptance: provider config is validated and credential references are redacted
backend health/probe APIs distinguish unavailable, degraded, and ready
model pull streams progress with stable event schema
embedded/local backends default safe and optional
anti_patterns: remote model call required for local-first workflows
streaming progress shape differs between API and client
manual_simulation: Configure local backend, probe health, pull model with progress, run inference, then break backend and inspect errors.
incentive: Inference is useful only when optional, observable, and locally controllable.

title: Repository and connector public API PRD
intent: Define repository browse/sync/tree/file APIs, connector credentials/status, webhooks, and external import mapping while preserving local-first defaults.
acceptance: repo APIs expose local path, branches, tree, file content, and sync status safely
connector APIs use credential refs and status diagnostics
webhook endpoints validate signatures and record delivery events
external imports map fields with reviewable conflicts
anti_patterns: hosted integration required for core workflow
manual_simulation: Register local repo, browse file tree, sync external connector with credential ref, receive webhook, and inspect mapped tasks/docs.
incentive: Repositories and connectors feed real project context into workflows.

title: Transactional outbox and event producer/consumer PRD
intent: Define how services emit, persist, dispatch, retry, and consume domain events across audit, notifications, subscriptions, and workflow traces.
acceptance: service writes state mutation and event in one transaction where supported
PGlite fallback has documented non-transactional behavior
outbox retry and dead-letter behavior are observable
consumer map lists notification/audit/subscription/workflow consumers
anti_patterns: fire-and-forget event emit before DB commit
manual_simulation: Trigger task/comment/run event, crash dispatch once, restart worker, and verify exactly-once observable side effects or documented duplicate handling.
incentive: Cross-service workflows need durable events, not incidental callbacks.

title: Local seed and bootstrap data PRD
intent: Specify seed data ownership, idempotency, additive-only hooks, default org/user/project, notification defaults, and migration interaction.
acceptance: seed can run repeatedly without duplicate rows
default local workspace includes org/user/project/settings needed for first workflow
seed uses TypeORM repositories/entities, not raw SQL-only fixtures
seed records version/status for doctor visibility
anti_patterns: test-only seed drift from product seed
manual_simulation: Delete FULCRUM_HOME, start app, inspect seeded org/user/project/settings, rerun seed, and verify no duplicates.
incentive: First-run local state must be reliable for a local-first OS.

title: Unified DTO, Zod, and error response PRD
intent: Define validation and error mapping across Nest DTOs, Zod schemas, tRPC errors, HTTP errors, and service domain exceptions.
acceptance: invalid input returns stable field-level errors on HTTP and tRPC
domain exceptions map without leaking internals
DTOs/schemas do not use z.any for public contracts
Swagger documents request/response/error shapes
anti_patterns: different status code for same validation failure
manual_simulation: Send invalid payloads to project/task/docs/workflow endpoints through HTTP and tRPC and compare structured errors.
incentive: Reliable validation is the API contract users and agents build against.

title: Cross-service authorization and tenant isolation PRD
intent: Specify org/project/user permission enforcement for every controller, tRPC router, stream topic, and local caller path.
acceptance: every public API receives authenticated subject or explicit local trusted context
org/project filters are applied in stores before returning rows
stream topics enforce tenant scope
tests cover denied access for at least one endpoint per service
anti_patterns: controllers accepting orgId as trust boundary without session check
local caller bypass without explicit trust mode
stream topic guessed from client input
manual_simulation: Create two orgs, seed data in both, call APIs and streams as each user, and verify isolation plus denied mutations.
incentive: Local-first does not remove the need for tenant and project boundaries.

title: OpenAPI and API discoverability PRD
intent: Require every NestJS public API controller to expose tags, operation summaries, DTO bodies, response metadata, and auth/error docs.
acceptance: Swagger includes all mounted public controllers
operation summaries are responsibility-named and user-oriented
body/query/param DTOs are reflected accurately
error and auth response metadata exists for protected endpoints
anti_patterns: decorator application missing for generated descriptors
manual_simulation: Generate OpenAPI document, enumerate endpoints, compare to controller route inventory, and try generated client for workflow path.
incentive: Agents and humans need API affordances discoverable without reading source.

title: Generated and hand-written API client parity PRD
intent: Define HTTP API client behavior for web/CLI/TUI use, cookie forwarding, org/user scope, response normalization, and fallback local caller routing.
acceptance: each public controller has a typed client or generated client strategy
web server routes forward cookies and request context
CLI/TUI callers can switch between local in-process and configured HTTP
client tests cover field normalization without losing data
anti_patterns: route-specific fetch wrappers diverging from service client
manual_simulation: Call the same docs/tasks/workflow API from web server action, CLI, TUI, and direct HTTP client, then diff payloads.
incentive: Invocation layers need one contract per service, not bespoke adapters.

title: Local job queue and worker registry PRD
intent: Specify job queue entities, registry, metrics rollup, worker tick contracts, and local-first processing guarantees.
acceptance: jobs persist type, payload, status, attempts, schedule, and trace where applicable
workers are registered by responsibility and can be run locally
metrics rollup reports queue depth, failures, and latency
worker failures are retryable or terminal with reason
manual_simulation: Enqueue notification/artifact/dependency jobs, run worker registry, induce failure, and inspect metrics and retries.
incentive: Long-running local workflows need resumable background work.

title: Backup, restore, import, and export API PRD
intent: Define local backup runner, scheduled backups, remote adapters, data portability endpoints, and restore safety checks.
acceptance: backup captures database, artifacts, config, and selected local state
restore validates version/schema before applying
remote adapters are optional and credential-ref based
data portability export/import reports partial failures
anti_patterns: exports missing artifacts or trace edges
manual_simulation: Create workflow data and artifact, run backup, restore into fresh FULCRUM_HOME, and verify trace/workflow continuity.
incentive: Local-first products must make user data portable and recoverable.

title: Service module extraction readiness PRD
intent: Define extraction criteria for each services/* bounded service: module exports, interface controllers, application services, infrastructure isolation, and no app-surface business logic.
acceptance: each service exposes module/providers from service root or interface module
domain code imports no infrastructure
interface/http depends on application/services, not direct ORM where avoidable
web/CLI/TUI have no direct ORM or application-service business logic
anti_patterns: platform-core god module absorbing service entities
repositories exported as public module API
manual_simulation: Pick one service and sketch package extraction: package.json, exports, imports, and remaining cross-boundary references.
incentive: Microservice-splittable monorepo is an explicit architecture target.

title: PGlite and PostgreSQL persistence proof matrix PRD
intent: Define which API families require dual database tests, which use mocked unit tests, and how fixture schema drift is handled.
acceptance: each persisted public API family has PGlite coverage
critical workflow and migration paths also run PostgreSQL coverage
unit tests avoid database unless persistence behavior is under test
fixture schema patches are documented as test harness only
anti_patterns: PGlite-only passing proof for production-critical behavior
broad CI used instead of focused proof
manual_simulation: Build a matrix of controllers vs PGlite/PostgreSQL tests and run one representative gate per risk tier.
incentive: Database confidence must be explicit, not inferred from scattered tests.

title: Request ID, trace ID, telemetry, and error-log PRD
intent: Specify request ID propagation, trace ID linking, telemetry event recording, error log APIs, and remote telemetry opt-in behavior.
acceptance: every request has requestId and optional traceId in logs/errors
error log API supports list/detail/clear with org scope
telemetry is local by default and remote opt-in
requestId links HTTP, tRPC, audit, and error records
manual_simulation: Trigger validation error and workflow failure, inspect request/error/audit/trace records, then toggle telemetry settings.
incentive: Local operators need correlation without involuntary telemetry.

title: Review and workflow stream convergence PRD
intent: Define how ad hoc SvelteKit review SSE, Nest workflow live-feedback stream, tRPC streaming, and subscription events converge into one stream contract.
acceptance: all streams emit typed events with id, type, traceId, timestamp, payload
review stream either delegates to service stream or documents why HTTP-only
CLI/TUI watch modes consume same event schema
reconnect and last-event handling are specified
anti_patterns: one-off SSE route bypassing service events
stream event text assembled in UI route
watch commands polling different response shape
manual_simulation: Subscribe from web EventSource and CLI watch to same trace, trigger review/run events, disconnect/reconnect, and compare received events.
incentive: Live product UX should not fragment by route implementation.

title: Runtime lifecycle and graceful shutdown PRD
intent: Define server startup sequencing, database migrations, optional service startup, worker registration, Yjs/subscription servers, and graceful shutdown cleanup.
acceptance: startup order is deterministic and logged: config, DB, migrations, Nest, streams/workers
optional runtime components are feature flagged and health checked
shutdown closes HTTP server, DataSource, websocket servers, and background workers
startup failures produce actionable doctor/readiness state
anti_patterns: feature server started from module import side effect
manual_simulation: Start with collab/subscriptions enabled, run workflow, send shutdown, and verify no open handles or lost final events.
incentive: Long-running local app must start and stop predictably.

title: Public route taxonomy and versioning PRD
intent: Define `/api/v1/*`, `/workflows/*`, tRPC, stream, webhook, and internal route taxonomy so clients know stability and lifecycle.
acceptance: stable public APIs live under documented versioned prefixes
workflow orchestration routes have clear namespace and client wrappers
internal/runtime routes are marked non-public
versioning and deprecation policy is documented in generated API metadata
anti_patterns: new public route with unversioned path by accident
web-only API used by CLI/TUI as stable contract
webhook route mixed with internal command route
manual_simulation: Enumerate mounted routes, classify public/workflow/internal/webhook/stream, then generate client calls for each stable namespace.
incentive: A local Agent OS still needs a stable API product surface.
